examples.question_text: State the standard domain restriction of $y=\sin x$ used to define $y=\arcsin x$. Sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, symmetry, monotonicity and any asymptotes.
State the standard domain restriction of $y=\cos x$ used to define $y=\arccos x$. Sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, endpoints, symmetry, monotonicity and any asymptotes.

State the standard domain restriction of $y=\tan x$ used to define $y=\tan^{-1}x$. Explain this notation, then sketch the inverse graph and state its domain, range, symmetry, monotonicity and asymptotes.
By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=6+\cos x$ for $0\le x\le\pi$. State the inverse's domain and range.
examples.solution_text:
Swap $x$ and $y$, then isolate cosine.

$\begin{aligned}x&=6+\cos y\\x-6&=\cos y\\y&=\arccos(x-6)\end{aligned}$

The original range is $5\le y\le7$, so the inverse domain is $5\le x\le7$. The inverse range is the original restricted domain, $0\le y\le\pi$.

examples.question_text: By swapping $x$ and $y$, find the inverse of $y=7-6\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$ for $-\pi\le x\le\pi$. State the inverse's domain and range.
examples.solution_text:
The restriction gives $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le\frac{x}{2}\le\frac{\pi}{2}$, so sine is one-to-one. Swap the variables and isolate sine before applying its inverse.

$\begin{aligned}x&=7-6\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\x-7&=-6\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\\frac{7-x}{6}&=\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)\\\frac{y}{2}&=\arcsin\left(\frac{7-x}{6}\right)\\y&=2\arcsin\left(\frac{7-x}{6}\right)\end{aligned}$

The original range is $1\le y\le13$, so the inverse domain is $1\le x\le13$. The inverse range is $-\pi\le y\le\pi$.

examples.derivation: Restricted sine increases from -1 to 1 on [-π/2,π/2]. Exchanging coordinates gives inverse domain [-1,1], range [-π/2,π/2] and endpoints (-1,-π/2), (1,π/2). Sine's oddness gives inverse oddness. The plotted coordinates (sin(t),tπ/180), for t from -90 to 90 degrees, reproduce arcsin with included endpoints and no asymptotes.

Restricted cosine decreases from 1 to -1 on [0,π]. Its inverse therefore decreases on [-1,1], with range [0,π] and endpoints (-1,π), (1,0). The nonzero value arccos(0)=π/2 excludes oddness; unequal values at ±1 exclude evenness. The plotted coordinates (cos(t),tπ/180), for t from 0 to 180 degrees, match these properties.

Tangent is increasing and odd on (-π/2,π/2), with range all real numbers. Its inverse consequently has real domain, strict range (-π/2,π/2), increasing behaviour and odd symmetry. Its limits at positive and negative infinity are ±π/2. TikZ atan(t) returns degrees, so multiplication by π/180 correctly plots radians; dashed lines mark the two horizontal asymptotes.

Swapping variables gives x=6+cos(y), hence cos(y)=x-6 and y=arccos(x-6). On the original domain [0,π], cosine ranges from 1 to -1, giving original range [5,7]. The inverse domain is [5,7] and its range is [0,π]. Independent equations align at their equality signs; no phantom gutter or diagram is needed.

The original restriction makes x/2 lie in [-π/2,π/2]. Swapping variables gives x=7-6sin(y/2), so sin(y/2)=(7-x)/6 and y=2arcsin((7-x)/6). Original endpoint outputs are 13 and 1, giving inverse domain [1,13] and range [-π,π]. Independent equations align correctly without phantom equals; no diagram is needed.
